brief:
Create a coherent, parametric Mini F1 concept assembly in Fusion 360 consisting of exactly four main components:

1. **MON-001 — Monocoque:** A tapered central chassis with a raised cockpit rim, an open cockpit, a narrow front nose and a wider rear section.
2. **FWG-001 — Front Wing:** A multi-element front wing with a main plane, two simplified flaps and endplates, mounted ahead of the monocoque.
3. **FLR-001 — Floor:** A broad, thin aerodynamic floor beneath the chassis, with simplified side edges and a tapered rear diffuser ramp.
4. **RWG-001 — Rear Wing:** A raised rear wing with a main plane, one flap, two endplates and simplified supports.

Use millimetres and the project coordinate convention: +X forward, +Y left, +Z upward, with the origin on the front-axle centreline and Z=0 on the reference plane.

Design the four components as separate, editable Fusion components in one design. Place them in a coherent vehicle layout with no unintended solid intersections. Use named features and meaningful user parameters where practical. Keep the shapes manufacturable-looking and geometrically simple enough to regenerate reliably.

Develop a dimensioned concept plan first. Use only the FIA rule excerpts supplied by the system; do not invent rule dimensions or claim FIA compliance. Mark unsupported dimensions as assumptions. Prioritise a successful complete assembly, correct component placement, valid solids, and clear front, top and isometric views over excessive geometric detail.

Connections: parts connect by face contact, never by overlap. The front wing mount touches the nose tip, the monocoque sits on the top face of the floor, and the rear wing supports touch the rear of the monocoque (or the floor). Report the measured gap or overlap of every connected pair.
Keep every part within the overall vehicle width limit given in the supplied rules.
Scale (my own concept assumption, not a regulation value): roughly full-size F1 proportions, overall length about 5.5 m and overall width under 2 m.

Do not add extra main components beyond the four listed. If a critical design decision is missing, ask at most one blocking question; otherwise proceed with explicit assumptions.

At completion, report the component status, measured bounding boxes, placement and interference/gap checks, applicable FIA verification statuses, assumptions, and any failures. Generate isometric, front and top screenshots.

parts.name: Monocoque
parts.role: survival cell / chassis tub with nose and cockpit opening
parts.notes: Tapered loft from wide rear section (X=-3700, 900 wide x 700 high, Z 30-730) to narrow nose tip (X=+550, 200 wide x 200 high, Z 30-230, flat vertical tip face that the front wing mount touches). Flat bottom at Z=30 sits on floor top face. Open cockpit cut from top, approx X -2300 to -1500, 500 wide, with raised rim 60 mm high around opening. Flat vertical rear face at X=-3700 for rear wing supports. Half-width 450 is well inside the 950 mm limit.

parts.name: Front wing
parts.role: front wing: main plane, flap(s), endplates; ahead of the front axle
parts.notes: Main plane (chord 350, 30 thick) spanning 1800 at low Z (~70-100) at front X 800-1150; two flaps chord 180 stacked rearward/upward with small slot gaps, giving up to three sections per Y-plane. Two vertical endplates (20 thick, 280 high, Z 50-330) at Y=±880..±900. Central mount/pylon block Y ±60, from flap/main plane rearward to X=550, Z 100-230, its rear face touching the monocoque nose tip face (no overlap).

parts.name: Floor
parts.role: floor plate under the car with rear diffuser ramp
parts.notes: Thin flat plate X -4300 to -400, Y ±800, Z 0-30; top face Z=30 carries the monocoque. Simplified side edges: chamfered/tapered outer edges and slightly tapered front corners in plan. Rear diffuser ramp: wedge X -3700 to -4300, Y ±500, rising from Z=30 at X=-3700 to Z=230 at rear edge, behind the monocoque rear face so no intersection. Single solid body.

parts.name: Rear wing
parts.role: rear wing: main plane, flap, endplates, central support
parts.notes: Main plane chord 350 at Z ~870-905, X -4400 to -4050, span 1000 between endplates; one flap chord 200 above/behind with slot gap (Z ~930-1000). Two endplates 20 thick, Z 700-1100, X -4450 to -3950 at Y ±500..±520. Two simplified support plates (20 thick in Y, centred Y=±100) from front face at X=-3700 (touching monocoque rear face, Z 400-730 region) sweeping rearward up to the main plane underside. Clear of floor diffuser (max Z 230).

assumptions.text: Overall length ~5600 mm, from front wing leading edge X=+1150 to rear wing endplate trailing edge X=-4450.
Max part half-width set to 900 mm (front wing), inside the 950 mm limit of C2.3.1.
Floor is 30 mm thick with its top face at Z=30; the monocoque has a flat bottom at Z=30.
Monocoque runs from X=+550 (nose tip) to X=-3700 (rear face); the nose has a flat bottom with no raised-nose geometry.
Front wing mount is a central pylon block whose rear face touches the 200x200 nose tip face at X=550.
Rear wing uses two support plates at Y=±100 that touch the monocoque rear face at X=-3700, not a single pylon.
Diffuser ramp rises from 30 mm to 230 mm over the last 600 mm of the floor and is 1000 mm wide.
Wing profiles are simplified as constant-thickness cambered or flat plates; no RV/RS reference volumes are modelled.
